content.value_statement: Responsive interfaces often break across cards, grids, tables, and navigation. This skill supplies practical CSS and React patterns for fluid, component-aware layouts.
actual_capabilities: Designs mobile-first breakpoint strategies based on content needs.
Applies container queries for component-level responsive behavior.
Creates fluid typography and spacing scales with CSS clamp().
Builds responsive CSS Grid, Flexbox, navigation, image, and table patterns.
Recommends fallbacks, feature queries, and viewport unit choices.
limitations: Does not test layouts on real devices unless the host agent runs browser checks.
Does not replace accessibility, performance, or visual regression testing.
Does not provide a complete design system by itself.
Requires project-specific content, components, and browser support targets.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Marketing Page
use_cases.description: Turn fixed-width sections into fluid layouts with responsive typography, images, and grid behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize Design System Breakpoints
use_cases.description: Define practical breakpoint tokens, container query rules, and layout guidance for reusable components.

use_cases.title: Improve Data Views on Mobile
use_cases.description: Adapt dense tables and dashboards into scrollable, card-based, or container-aware layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Page Responsive
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one page or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page and make it responsive for mobile, tablet, and desktop. Use mobile-first CSS and explain the main layout changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Fluid Type and Spacing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for typography and spacing tokens.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a fluid typography and spacing scale for this interface. Use clamp() with clear minimum and maximum values.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to Container Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor these reusable components to use container queries where appropriate. Keep viewport media queries only where they are still needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Responsive System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a design system or large product surface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this responsive design system for breakpoint quality, overflow risk, fluid scaling, component reuse, and fallback behavior. Provide prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: A product grid uses four fixed columns and overflows on phones.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a mobile-first auto-fit grid, a minimum card width, fluid gaps, and testing at narrow content widths.

output_examples.input: A dashboard card works in the main area but fails inside a narrow sidebar.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest container queries so the card adapts to its parent width instead of the viewport.

output_examples.input: A data table is unreadable on small screens.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare horizontal scrolling with a mobile card layout and recommend the option that preserves scanning and labels.

best_practices: Start from mobile styles, then enhance for wider screens and richer containers.
Set breakpoints where content breaks, not only at common device widths.
Use fluid values with minimum and maximum bounds for type, spacing, and media.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on fixed desktop widths and patch mobile behavior afterward.
Do not create many device-specific breakpoints without content reasons.
Do not use 100vh on mobile without considering dynamic viewport units.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build responsive layouts, components, typography, navigation, images, tables, and design system breakpoint rules.

faq.question: Does it use container queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes container query patterns for cards, grids, dashboards, navigation, and Tailwind-style workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with React?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples include TSX component patterns for responsive cards, grids, navigation, images, and tables.

faq.question: Does it replace browser testing?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance, but real viewport, device, accessibility, and regression testing are still needed.

faq.question: How does it choose breakpoints?
faq.answer: It favors content-based breakpoints, mobile-first rules, feature queries, and fluid layout techniques over device-only assumptions.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Tailwind breakpoint concepts and container query examples that can guide utility-based implementations.
